title: Canonical small-presentation coefficient ring and derived completion
statement: Let $\ell$ be prime and $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ a finite extension [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], with $E$ in any universe independently of the scheme $X$. Let $E^s=\operatorname{Shrink} E$ be its canonical small presentation, with field and algebra structures transported along the canonical algebra equivalence $E^s\simeq E$, and spectral norm. Put $\underline{\mathcal O_{E^s}}(S)=C(S,\mathcal O_{E^s})$, using the condensed continuous-ring construction [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], and $R_X=p_X^*\underline{\mathcal O_{E^s}}$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Form internal modules and their unbounded derived category [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. Define the positive-level reduction rings $B_{n,X}=p_X^*\underline{\mathcal O_{E^s}/\pi^{n+1}}$ and their canonical quotient transitions. Derived completeness on this presentation is the condition of [sk-def-pe-derived-completion]: for a K-flat representative $P$ of $K$, the specified augmentation $(c,0):P\to\operatorname{Roos}(P\otimes_{R_X}B_{n,X})$ becomes invertible in the derived category, where $c$ consists of the tensor-unit maps, the Roos differential is $(x,y)\mapsto(dx,(1-s)x-dy)$, and $s$ is induced by the quotient transitions. The canonical derived reduction functors, their transition maps, and normalized towers are formed by derived extension and exact restriction of scalars. A tower is normalized when the transition-induced comparison after extension from level $n+2$ to level $n+1$ is invertible. This is a presentation of the recorded completion notion, not an additional condition on $E$ or $K$.

source.place: canonical reduction comparison and normalized towers, using finite-dimensional smallness in the integral-heart coefficient setting
